1. Build the standard superpermutation (fast, ~5913 length)
2. Convert to a sequence of n-windows (edges in the De Bruijn graph of order n)
3. Use a more efficient deletion strategy: identify "redundant" windows (those appearing ≥2 times) and try removing their internal symbols in a targeted way, using a sliding window verification that's much faster than full re-verification

The key insight: when we delete a symbol at position `pos`, only windows `pos-n+1` through `pos` are affected. We can check if any of those windows was the *only* occurrence of its permutation. This makes each deletion test O(n) instead of O(n·n!).
